analysis.headline: US intelligence backed a Venezuelan drone strike on an ELN camp in Apure, and Washington is negotiating a long-term military deal with Caracas
analysis.what_happened: El País reports a drone strike on an ELN base in Apure, on the Colombian border, killed at least 20 people, citing human rights groups. La Silla Vacía and The New York Times report US officials say Washington supplied intelligence.
analysis.says_vs_does: Earlier reports framed the strike as a Venezuelan army action, while El País calls it a US antidrug war on Venezuelan soil. La Silla Vacía separately names Tren de Aragua chief Niño Guerrero in Bolívar state as a target, so accounts of the operation differ.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The post-Maduro government gains standing with Washington by hitting a guerrilla it long hosted. CiberCuba and BAE Negocios report talks on a permanent US military presence, after a joint June strike killed Tren de Aragua founder Héctor Guerrero Flores.
tensions: Venezuelan state vs ELN: a former rear-guard host now strikes the guerrilla with US help.
US vs Tren de Aragua: joint strikes have now targeted its founders inside Venezuela.

analysis.headline: Forced recruitment across four states feeds the Sinaloa Cartel's civil war as Mazatlán closes its deadliest month
analysis.what_happened: El Universal reports a forced-recruitment network feeding the Sinaloa war from Jalisco, Zacatecas and Durango. Disappearances of non-residents in Sinaloa rose from 142 in 2023 to 231 in 2025, a 63% increase.
analysis.says_vs_does: Mazatlán mayor Estrella Palacios calls security 'a challenge' after October passed 100 homicides, Ríodoce reports. Ríodoce also reports a severed head left with a message addressed to her father.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure for recruitment payments or the factions' war spending.
analysis.at_stake: Both factions replace losses with outside recruits, and Infobae reports cells defecting from the Chapitos to seek new alliances. Culiacán's bishop says a priest was held and tortured for three days by captors seeking faction information.
tensions: Chapitos and CJNG vs Mayiza: El Universal links the Jalisco–Zacatecas route to the Chapitos–CJNG alliance and the Durango route to the Mayiza.
Factions vs the Church: torturers sought intelligence on Chapitos and Mayiza from a priest, the bishop says.

analysis.headline: The Navy arrests El Semáforo, successor to El Tanque in the CJNG, as El Mencho's brother asks a US judge for 20 years
analysis.what_happened: Milenio reports El Semáforo, the presumed successor of El Tanque in the CJNG, was detained in Tuxtepec, Oaxaca, 23 days after his former boss's capture. The Navy reports hits on CJNG, Los Salazar and Cártel de Guasave leaders between 14 and 28 October.
analysis.says_vs_does: Antonio Oseguera, Tony Montana, pleaded guilty to drug and weapons charges and asks for 20 years, citing health and age, Milenio and Infobae report. The Navy's tally is its own claim of results.
analysis.follow_the_money: The Navy values two Sinaloa seizures of vehicles, weapons and drugs at 6.182 million pesos, an official estimate of losses to the groups. Sources do not give other figures.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG, in succession since El Mencho's death, keeps losing regional commanders in quick succession. Oseguera's sentence sets the US price for a founding family member who pleaded guilty.
tensions: Navy vs CJNG: successive arrests in Oaxaca hit the same regional command twice in under a month.

analysis.headline: A US court sentences Chinese national Wenshen Xu to 12 years for laundering more than $22 million in CJNG drug proceeds
analysis.what_happened: Voz reports a US federal court sentenced Wenshen Xu, a 52-year-old Chinese citizen, to 12 years. His network moved more than 450 kilograms of cocaine into the United States and laundered more than $22 million.
analysis.says_vs_does: Mexico's Finance Ministry says the FATF evaluation that just ended reflected its anti-laundering efforts, El Economista reports. That is a government claim; the FATF's own findings are not in these sources.
analysis.follow_the_money: Over $22 million in drug proceeds was laundered through Xu's network on behalf of CJNG trafficking, according to the sentencing reported by Voz. Sources do not give dates for the flows.
analysis.at_stake: The case adds a court record to US claims that Chinese brokers launder cartel revenue. Mexico's FATF rating affects how foreign banks treat Mexican correspondent accounts.
tensions: US prosecutors vs Chinese money brokers: a conviction rather than a designation ties a Chinese national to CJNG proceeds.

analysis.headline: Colombia's House advances De la Espriella's Ley de Sometimiento as armed groups bomb police posts and toll booths
analysis.what_happened: El Heraldo reports the House rejected a motion to shelve bill PL 433/26 by 93 to 45 and approved its report. Weekend attacks in Tolima, Cauca, Huila and Chocó killed seven and wounded over 20, El Tiempo reports.
analysis.says_vs_does: President De la Espriella says 'the false total peace has ended'. El Tiempo reports high-value targets remain out of reach, and a truck bomb hit a police station in El Tambo, Cauca, on Wednesday.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The surrender law offers armed groups a legal exit while the state escalates. The Antioquia government reports the Clan del Golfo in 94 municipalities, up 40 since 2022.
tensions: Government vs FARC dissidents and ELN: attacks on police and toll booths in the southwest continue, with three toll attacks in under a month.
Clan del Golfo vs dissidents and ELN: the Clan holds 72% of Antioquia against 21 dissident and 17 ELN municipalities.

analysis.headline: Brazil's Senate passes the public security amendment unopposed as federal police target a PCC-linked group that moved R$500 million
analysis.what_happened: The Senate approved without opposition a constitutional amendment widening the federal government's security role against factions such as the PCC and CV. Revista Oeste reports the Federal Police targeted a PCC-linked group on the Paraguay border.
analysis.says_vs_does: Senators present the amendment as a blow to the factions, while the Federal Police case shows police officers suspected of aiding the PCC-linked scheme.
analysis.follow_the_money: The PCC-linked group allegedly moved R$500 million and ran drug routes to Europe, Revista Oeste reports. Sources do not give dates for the flows.
analysis.at_stake: Brasília gains authority over a security field held by the states. In Bolivia, police report expelling 65 PCC and CV leaders, while one faction still operates in Santa Cruz, Beni and the Chapare.
tensions: Federal government vs PCC: a border network with alleged police help sits inside the new federal mandate.

analysis.headline: Ecuador's El Oro province breaks its homicide record as Los Choneros and Sao Box fight Los Lobos for Machala
analysis.what_happened: Primicias reports El Oro has broken its homicide record, with Puerto Bolívar holding 11% of the killings and 300 families displaced. Police and Interior Ministry reports identify a Los Choneros and Sao Box alliance in Machala, Pasaje and Santa Rosa.
analysis.says_vs_does: President Noboa governs through states of exception three weeks before elections, Estrella Digital reports, yet official reports show violence rising in El Oro.
analysis.follow_the_money: Official reports cited by Primicias put drug sales points at USD 2,000 a day. Sources do not give a provincial total.
analysis.at_stake: Puerto Bolívar is an export port, so control of local plazas also bears on cocaine shipments. Ecuador has extradited nine nationals since a 2024 referendum allowed it.
tensions: Los Choneros and Sao Box vs Los Lobos and Lobos Espejo: they compete for Machala, Pasaje and Santa Rosa.

The House rejected shelving the Ley de Sometimiento by 93 to 45 while weekend attacks in four departments killed seven people.
A US court sentenced Chinese national Wenshen Xu to 12 years for a CJNG-linked network that laundered more than $22 million.
